confidence_meta.reason: FOMC decision lands today at 2:00pm ET / 8:00pm CEST, now only ~1.5-2 hours out -- -8%. The China DUV chip-tool shock enters a 4th session (KOSPI closed -5.98%, EWY now -5.32% further intraday, gap to its 20-day SMA widening to -16.4%), contagion outcome still unresolved -- -8%. MOVE stayed below 80 (76.09, no penalty per the formula), though VIX itself spiked +11.15% intraday -- a real increase in near-term uncertainty that the confidence formula doesn't directly capture since it keys off MOVE, not VIX. Scores not a clean 2-2 split (3 deteriorating -- credit, inflation, vol; 1 stable -- liquidity). Numeric confidence is unchanged vs this morning's pull, but the intraday tape (VIX spike, oil surge, curve-wide yield backup, SPY/QQQ/SOXX all reversing to red) argues for treating this print as a floor, not a settled read, pending the decision.

bias: Conditions re-tightened sharply today after two mornings of relative calm: nominal yields backed up across the entire curve (2s through 30s all up 0.7-1.3%), oil extended its reversal to +7.18% (nearly double this morning's already-sharp bounce), and VIX spiked +11.15% -- closing the 2-day gap between calming US vol and the deepening Korea/AI-memory shock that this monitor flagged explicitly this morning. Credit softened at the margin (COF reversed to -0.75%, ALLY weakened) but did not blow out -- HY OAS held flat at 2.81%, and CACC kept firming. Breakevens (T5YIE, T10YIE) stayed calm despite the oil surge, and USDKRW remains comfortably below the BOK watch line, so this reads more as pre-FOMC positioning and event risk than a new systemic credit or FX event. The Korea/DUV chip-tool shock is now in a 4th session with no sign of stabilizing -- EWY's gap to its 20-day average has widened further intraday. The FOMC decision and Kevin Warsh's press conference in roughly two hours are the swing factor for whether today's move extends or reverses.

counterargs.thesis: A curve-wide yield backup, oil surge, and VIX spike suggest risk-off is intensifying into FOMC, layered on top of an unresolved, 4th-session Korea/AI-memory shock
supporting: US10Y through US30Y all rose 0.7-1.3% today -- a genuine curve-wide backup, not an isolated move
Oil +7.18% intraday, nearly double this morning's +3.77% bounce -- a large, hard-to-ignore one-day move
VIX +11.15% to 20.23 -- the clearest single-day vol move this cycle, resolving the prior 2-day US-vol/Korea-rout decoupling
SPY -1.16%, QQQ -1.71%, SOXX -4.96% -- broad US equities and semis both red, no longer just a Korea-specific story
EWY -5.32% further intraday on top of a 3-session rout; gap to its SMA20 now -16.4%, the widest yet
against: HY OAS still flat at 2.81% -- no credit-spread widening despite the equity/vol stress
CACC still firming (+1.61%) -- credit proxies are mixed, not uniformly deteriorating
Breakevens (T5YIE, T10YIE) still calm/slightly lower despite the oil surge -- no genuine inflation-expectations unanchoring
USDKRW still comfortably below the 1,530 BOK line -- zero FX contagion from the Korea rout
Gold fell -0.49% -- not the commodity/flight-to-safety pattern a true inflation or crisis scare would typically show
MOVE unchanged at 76.09, still well below the 80 stress line -- bond-market vol hasn't confirmed the equity-vol spike
counterargs.read: Today looks like a genuine, broad-based risk-off day -- yields up everywhere, oil surging, VIX spiking, and US equities/semis joining the Korea rout for the first time in several sessions. But credit spreads, breakevens, and the KRW have not moved with it, which argues this is concentrated in rates and equity-vol positioning ahead of a binary FOMC decision rather than a new systemic credit or inflation event. The next 1-2 hours (the decision itself and Warsh's press conference) will likely determine whether today's move extends into a genuine regime shift or partially reverses as event risk clears.

duration_score.classification: Curve-Wide Yield Backup Into FOMC -- Broad Real-Rate Pressure, Not the Classic Sticky-Front-End Pain Trade
duration_score.reason: Unlike the textbook James pain trade (sticky nominal 2Y + collapsing 2Y breakeven), today shows ALL maturities rising together (2s through 30s, +0.7-1.3%) alongside a VIX spike and an oil surge to +7.18%. This is a broader, curve-wide repricing -- consistent with pre-FOMC positioning and event risk -- rather than a narrow real-rate story. It's negative for duration (TLT -0.55%) and a genuine deterioration from this morning, but credit hasn't blown out and breakevens are still calm, keeping it short of a 'very negative' recession-style read.

james_framework.what_market_IS_saying: The whole curve is backing up into the FOMC decision rather than just the front end -- a broader repricing of term premium/event risk than the narrow sticky-2Y pattern
james_framework.pain_trade: Real 2Y proxy (US02Y - EXPINF2YR) rose to ~1.894% from ~1.853% this morning -- real-rate pressure is building, but via rising nominal yields across the curve rather than collapsing breakevens specifically
james_framework.watch_signal: If yields broadly reverse lower post-FOMC (dovish hold or dovish guidance), this unwinds quickly; a hawkish Warsh tone alongside the oil surge could extend the real-rate pressure
